headline: Two drown in pond at Jagannath University's second campus in Keraniganj
summary: Two women drowned while bathing in a pond at Jagannath University's second campus in Keraniganj. The incident occurred on Monday afternoon, prompting the university to issue a notice restricting public access to the pond.
details: Two women, Julia (20) and Rabeya (14), tragically drowned while bathing in a pond at Jagannath University's second campus in Tegharia, Keraniganj, on Monday afternoon. They were among four women who had entered the pond.
Local residents recovered their bodies after the incident. Inspector Abul Kalam Azad of South Keraniganj Police Station confirmed the deaths, stating that legal procedures are currently underway.

Following the tragedy, Jagannath University's Vice-Chancellor, Rais Uddin, announced that a notice has been issued to limit public entry to the pond. The notice warns that legal action will be taken against anyone entering or staying at the ghat without prior permission.

headline: KCC announces Tk 601.79cr budget for FY 2026-27
summary: Khulna City Corporation has announced a Tk 601.79 crore budget for the current fiscal year, focusing on waste management, mosquito control, and waterlogging solutions without imposing new taxes.
details: Khulna City Corporation (KCC) has officially announced a proposed budget of Tk 601.79 crore for the current fiscal year. The budget was declared by KCC Administrator Nazrul Islam Monju.
The announced budget projects a revenue income of Tk 211.90 crore, with an overall operating expenditure estimated at Tk 241.44 crore.
Additionally, the City Corporation anticipates receiving Tk 197.62 crore in general grants from the government. An extra Tk 79.46 crore is expected as a grant under special development projects.

Administrator Nazrul Islam Monju assured citizens that no new taxes would be imposed. The budget prioritizes waste management and mosquito eradication to enhance citizen facilities and improve living standards.

Special allocations have been made to permanently resolve waterlogging, a long-standing issue for Khulna residents. This includes repairing internal city roads and modernizing and expanding the drainage system on a priority basis.

Khulna City Corporation has unveiled a Tk 601.79 crore budget for the current fiscal year. No new taxes will be imposed on citizens.

Khulna City Corporation (KCC) has officially announced a proposed budget of Tk 601.79 crore for the current fiscal year. The budget was declared by KCC Administrator Nazrul Islam Monju.

The announced budget projects a revenue income of Tk 211.90 crore, with an overall operating expenditure estimated at Tk 241.44 crore.

Additionally, the City Corporation anticipates receiving Tk 197.62 crore in general grants from the government. An extra Tk 79.46 crore is expected as a grant under special development projects.

Administrator Nazrul Islam Monju assured citizens that no new taxes would be imposed. The budget prioritizes waste management and mosquito eradication to enhance citizen facilities and improve living standards.

Special allocations have been made to permanently resolve waterlogging, a long-standing issue for Khulna residents. This includes repairing internal city roads and modernizing and expanding the drainage system on a priority basis.
